chapter: Then versus now, dances and carnival balls
title: Drumming then and now: more feeling in the old days
summary: Old drummers expressed feeling and showed it; modern drummers stick to a regular beat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And do you notice any difference between the music then and now or the drumming then and now?

Well, I knew... The only difference I could see from then, from that time and now, is the music... The drums are a little more modernistic. In other words, look like they're beat more... More modern. But for a feeling... ...

Those drummers at that time, to me, they had more feeling than the drummers. You take the drummers at that time, they'd be playing, they'd be doing everything. They'd be making all kinds of motions. They'd be expressing their feelings. They'd be playing to show you what they're feeling. For the drummers nowadays, they look like they're playing more modernistic. They play more different from the guys who play that. I don't know, somehow they don't have much feelings as the guys are doing that. Of course, they play now. They play a lot of drums now. It looks to me that the drummers don't have the feelings that the drummers had in those days. Because those days, the drummer, if he knew something, he always did it. If he was throwing the sticks around, if he was hitting on the side of the bass drum, either the drummers would hit on the side of the drum stand. They'd make all those kind of things at that time. But now the drummers, he's got some modernistic now to let those things go by. They stick to their own set. They stick to their regular beat.
You think it's more like mechanical.
Yeah, that's right. But there are a lot of them playing now. They're playing a lot of drums.
